source: Area: Encyclopaedia Britannica · Convention on the Legal Status of the Caspian Sea (2018)

beats.say: The world's biggest lake is called a sea.
beats.title: THIS 'SEA' IS ACTUALLY A LAKE

beats.say: The Caspian Sea has no connection to any ocean. Water only leaves by evaporating.
It covers about three hundred seventy one thousand square kilometers. That's bigger than Germany.
Five countries share its shore: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
Sea or lake actually matters. Under it lie huge oil and gas fields, and the label decides who gets what.
In twenty eighteen, the five countries signed a deal giving it a special status. Officially, it's neither.
A lake that's too big to be a lake. Follow for more.
beats.title: TOO BIG TO BE A LAKE
